description: Start with Non-Lucrative, Work, Student, or Digital Nomad basics. Confirm which options apply to your situation.

title: Confirm your consulate jurisdiction (where you must apply)

title: Choose the appropriate visa type for your situation
Research cost of living in different Spanish cities/regions
Decide on a target city or region in Spain
description: Consider jobs/schools, healthcare access, climate, transit, and housing costs.

title: Start learning Spanish (apps, courses, tutors)
Estimate monthly budget and proof-of-funds requirements
description: Calculate required savings/income for your chosen visa and your family size. Build a conservative buffer.

title: Ensure passport is valid for at least 6 months beyond intended stay
Request certified copies of birth/marriage certificates (if needed)
description: Many consulates require certified copies, plus apostille and sworn translations depending on your case.

title: Plan apostille and sworn translation timeline
description: Apostilles and sworn translations can take weeks. Confirm which documents require each.

title: Complete visa application form (specific to consulate)
description: Fill the long-stay visa form required by your consulate.

title: Obtain passport-sized photos (meeting specifications)
Gather proof of financial means (bank statements, investments)
Secure Spanish-compliant health insurance
description: Confirm it meets consulate requirements (often: full coverage, no co-pays, valid for Spain, for the required duration).

title: Obtain medical certificate (apostilled if required by consulate)
Obtain police clearance certificate (FBI background check, apostilled)
Arrange proof of accommodation in Spain (rental, hotel, invitation letter)
Get sworn translations of necessary documents (if not in Spanish)
Pay the visa application fee
Schedule visa appointment at the Spanish consulate
Submit visa application and attend interview (if required)
Track visa application status
Receive visa approval and collect passport with visa
Book flights to Spain
Arrange temporary accommodation in Spain for arrival (if needed)
Secure long-term housing (if not done)
Notify US banks and credit card companies of travel/move
Set up mail forwarding in the US
Digitize and securely store important documents
description: Keep encrypted backups (passport, visa, apostilles, insurance, bank statements, birth certificates).

title: Sell, donate, or store belongings in the US
Arrange shipping of essential items to Spain
Obtain an International Driving Permit (IDP)
Plan cancellation of US utilities, phone, and subscriptions
Pack essentials for arrival and initial weeks
Arrive in Spain
Register on the Padrón (Empadronamiento) at your local town hall
description: You’ll often need the padrón certificate for TIE, school enrollment, and some utilities.

title: Obtain NIE (Número de Identificación de Extranjero) if not issued with visa
description: Often handled alongside the TIE process. Required for most admin tasks.

Obtain TIE — fill out EX-17 application form
Obtain TIE — pay TASA 790-012 fee

Phase 5: Long-Term Setup & Ongoing Compliance — Start
description: Long-term admin tasks that keep life smooth: taxes, digital identity, renewals, school, and ongoing compliance.

title: Set up Cl@ve (digital identity) for online government services
description: Cl@ve helps you use Spanish public administration portals for appointments, taxes, and paperwork.

title: Create a system for storing and renewing residency documents
description: Track renewal deadlines for TIE, insurance policies, passport expiration, and required supporting documents.

title: Confirm your tax residency status and obligations (Spain + US)
description: If you live in Spain long enough, you may become a Spanish tax resident. Understand timelines, reporting, and US filing overlap.

title: Choose a Spanish tax advisor (gestor) if your situation is complex
description: Recommended if you have US income, investments, self-employment, or multiple countries involved.

title: Set up recurring bill payments (utilities, rent/mortgage, mobile, insurance)
description: Use direct debit (domiciliación) where appropriate to avoid missed payments and admin friction.

title: Register children for school or childcare (if applicable)
description: Confirm enrollment requirements, local zoning/catchment rules, and required documents.

title: Enroll with a dentist / pediatrician and set up routine care schedule
description: Get established before you need urgent care. Keep insurance and referral rules handy.

title: If staying longer than 6 months, plan long-term driving requirements
description: Confirm whether you must exchange, re-test, or obtain a Spanish license depending on your situation and bilateral agreements.

title: Set up local registrations and accounts (libraries, transit cards, local services)
description: Small upgrades that dramatically improve daily life and reduce friction.

title: Review insurance coverage annually (health, renters/home, liability)
description: As your residency and life changes, your insurance needs change too.

title: Phase 5: Long-Term Setup & Ongoing Compliance — Complete
description: You’ve built the boring-but-powerful foundation: compliance, stability, and fewer surprises.
